page: Vultr voc-m-16c-128gb-1600s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores on an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, this server includes 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled as a local 1600 GB NVMe SSD. The CPU architecture supports hardware-level features such as AVX, AES, SHA_NI, and BMI2, though it lacks AVX-512 extensions.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance exhibits a distinct performance profile. Its single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng, ranks in the top tier (top 10%), whereas multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores fall within the average tier (middle 50%). Memory performance is a notable strength, with PassMark memory scores ranking in the top 25%, despite uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidths remaining in the average tier at 131.64 GB/sec and 67.64 GB/sec respectively. Database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput also align with average tier benchmarks.

The hardware configuration offers high resource density, particularly regarding memory and local NVMe storage, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-heavy workloads that do not require GPU acceleration. However, the 2.0 GHz clock speed and average multi-core scaling represent a tradeoff for compute-bound parallel processing. This server is suited for memory-intensive databases, medium-scale Redis deployments, static web serving, and lightweight LLM inference tasks, such as running a 7B parameter model where text generation reaches 20.15 tokens per second.
